title: mixed-workload soak + burst profiling and p95 regression detector
creator: Asha Patel
description: Goal: Build a repeatable, mixed-workload soak and burst test harness for Dedicated capacity that measures tokens/sec, tail latencies (p95/p99), and detects regressions in throughput/latency profiles. This ticket covers test definition, harness extension, statistical regression detector, and automation to run backfills nightly and on-demand for PR validation. The harness must support steady-state traffic, controlled sustained bursts, burst-with-decay, and spike-multiplexed scenarios across multiple model classes (small/medium/large) and request payloads (short prompts, long prompts, embeddings).
acceptance_criteria: A reusable load harness can run a mixed workload scenario for >= 6 hours on Dedicated clusters and produce artifacts: per-second tokens, p50/p95/p99 latency, error-rate, and GPU utilization timelines
A regression detector runs on historical windows and flags p95 or tokens/sec regressions with an actionable signal (pass/fail) and confidence score
Automated nightly runs produce a JSON report and upload to the regression dashboard S3 path and create alerts for high-severity regressions
The harness allows toggling KV cache warm/cold states, simulating different cache hit rates, and produces separate breakdowns for warm vs cold requests
Runbook documenting how to run the scenario locally and in CI is added to Confluence and linked from the ticket
test_plan: Scenario definitions: steady-state (constant arrival, 80% short prompts, 20% long prompts), sustained-burst (10x baseline for 10 minutes every hour), spike-decay (60s sharp spike then exponential backoff), mixed-tenant (interleaved request streams representing 5 tenants)
Traffic generator changes: implement token-aware request sizing, Poisson arrival process option, and per-tenant rate-multipliers
Instrumenting agents: emit per-request tokens, model-variant, KV-cache-state, and backend queue time to trace headers
Measurement windows: compute rolling 1m and 5m quantiles for p95 and tokens/sec; store raw time-series and aggregated summaries
Regression detector: initial algorithm = CUSUM on p95 with EWMA baseline and bootstrap to estimate significance; configurable sensitivity for nightly vs PR runs
Validation: run synthetic regressions (inject +20% latency and -30% throughput) to verify detector true-positive rate and false-positive control
implementation_notes: Extend existing loadgen to accept new profile YAMLs (arrival distribution, token distribution, payload mix) and to emit structured JSON lines for each request
Add a lightweight post-processor that computes per-second tokens and quantiles and writes to S3 with timestamped keys
Reuse metrics ingestion: push aggregated metrics to existing Prometheus path and upload raw-results to s3://redwood-ci/dedicated-soak/
Implement detector as a separate service binary so it can be run from CI and as a nightly job; CLI accepts two windows: baseline (past N days) and candidate (latest run)
Detector output must include: metric name, baseline summary, candidate summary, delta, p-value, confidence, and recommended action (none/warn/fail)
Security: ensure loadgen keys use a test-only API key scope and that CI uploads are scrubbed of customer-identifying metadata
metrics_to_capture: request_latency_ms (p50, p95, p99) by model and payload-type
blockers: Need stable Dedicated cluster with deterministic autoscale controls from infra (ETA 2026-03-05)
Client SDK change for token-count metadata needs sign-off from SDK owners
